espn-603993.headline: One win this year, and none ever in Ireland
beats: Argentina have never won a Test in Ireland, and Ireland have never lost at home to them. Since beating Wales in July, Argentina's best result is a 28–28 draw with Australia in September.
Ireland last played in July and lost 21–40 in New Zealand. The win before that was 36–20 away to Japan. Andy Farrell's side need this one to stay in title contention.
Any Argentina win drops Ireland to fourth in the world, below France. These two could meet again in a World Cup quarter-final less than a year from now.
Fiji and Italy come next, both without a point after three rounds. Whoever wins in Dublin gets to enjoy that a little more.

espn-603994.headline: Italy have beaten South Africa once. It was ten years ago.
beats: It finished 20–18 in Florence on 19 November 2016, under Conor O'Shea, with South Africa at their lowest. O'Shea says he remembers it incredibly well. Italy's last attempt, on 15 November 2025, ended 14–32.
Italy lost all three July games without a point, conceding 131 along the way. Australia put 57 on them in July and 42 on South Africa in September. Only one of those sides lost by four.

Rassie Erasmus is not risking a repeat of 2016. He has named essentially the side that beat New Zealand, with Salmaan Moerat in for Eben Etzebeth. Gonzalo Quesada hands Samuele Locatelli a debut. An Italy win would drop South Africa to second, behind New Zealand.
The tenth anniversary falls twelve days after kickoff. Italy would settle for marking it early.

espn-603995.headline: Scotland's oldest unanswered question, asked again
beats: Scotland have never beaten New Zealand in 121 years of trying. At Murrayfield last November they trailed 17-0 at half-time, drew level at 17-17, and still lost 17–25.

New Zealand lost three straight to South Africa, conceding 43 in the last of them, then put 50 and 43 on Australia in October. Scotland's best day this year was 50–40 over France at home in March. Finn Russell and Sione Tuipulotu, the captain, are back for this one.
Win and Scotland go up to 5th in the world, above England. Dave Rennie has kept the status quo, with Codie Taylor, a centurion, as captain, so nothing will be handed over.
A week later Scotland host Australia and New Zealand go to Wales. Only one of those trips would feel lighter for what happened here.

espn-603996.headline: Last time it was one point. This time, two places
beats: Wales won 24–23 when Japan last came to Cardiff, on 15 November 2025, and the last four meetings have all been very close. Japan have still beaten Wales only twice.
They arrive without a fly-half they planned on. Sam Greene and Seung-sin Lee are injured, and Ryunosuke Ito, who started every Japan Test in 2026, is back at university for the whole tour.

Wales have not played since July, when South Africa beat them 43–0 without conceding a try's worth of reply. Japan lost 34–28 at home to Fiji on 24 October, and a win of any size here still puts them above Wales and drops Wales to 12th at best.
On 14 November Wales host New Zealand and Japan visit England. Cardiff is the easier of the two Saturdays, for both.

espn-603997.headline: Dupont and Ntamack together again, Fiji first in line
beats: Antoine Dupont and Romain Ntamack start together at half-back for the first time since March 2025. Dupont missed all of July with a calf problem. Ntamack's list runs longer, a long-running kidney problem included.
France put 42 on both Australia and Japan in July without Dupont. Fiji conceded 73 to England and 33 to Scotland that month, both at home, and sit last of twelve without a point.
Jake White, in his second game in charge, hands a Fiji Test debut to Nathan Hughes, a former England international. England are the side that put 73 on them.
Any defeat drops France below England in the world rankings. South Africa come to France next, which is the wrong week to start looking for half-backs again.

espn-603998.headline: Borthwick has his players' backing. Now he needs a win
beats: Jamie George and the returning captain Maro Itoje called a squad meeting on Friday over a Times article that portrays players fed up with Borthwick's man management. The senior players denied a rift and said they would "fight to protect" him.
The article had Ellis Genge clashing with Borthwick. Genge starts on the bench, behind Fin Baxter, who has two appearances since a 10-month foot injury.

Ben Curry, back after an injury-hit 16 months in place of his twin Tom, is picked to deal with Fraser McReight, who wins his 50th cap, and Carlo Tizzano. Australia conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October. Lose anyway, and England drop to seventh in the world, below Scotland and Australia.
The RFU has already said Borthwick stays through to next year's World Cup even if England flop. The players would rather nobody had to check.

espn-603999.headline: South Africa's No 1 rides on a Saturday-Friday turn
beats: South Africa play Italy in Turin and then France the following Friday. Schalk Burger called it "the tricky one". Last November they played France first and won 32–17.
South Africa have been first in the world only since 31 August. Lose here by any margin and New Zealand go above them, with France up to third.

South Africa's last Test was a 42–38 defeat in Australia, six tries scored and still beaten. France put 42 points on Australia and Japan in July with a side missing its Toulouse and Montpellier players.
South Africa go on to Ireland in Dublin either way. Whether they arrive as the world's best side is settled here.

espn-604000.headline: Italy have no points, and Fiji are next
beats: Three Nations Championship games, three defeats, a points difference of -94. Only Fiji sit below Italy, on the same zero, and they come to Italy the following Saturday.

Italy conceded 47 in New Zealand and 57 in Australia on consecutive Saturdays in July. Before Genova they meet South Africa in Turin without Tommaso Menoncello, a loss the Springbok assistant Mzwandile Stick called "a big loss for them".

Argentina are not arriving on a charge either. Their one win this year was 35–21 over Wales in July. Four games without one have followed, ending in a 28–28 draw at home to Australia, and they go to Dublin before this.
Win and Italy rise to ninth in the world, above Fiji and Wales. That would be a pleasant place to stand when Fiji arrive.

espn-604001.headline: Thirty-four in a row, and Cardiff has tickets left
beats: New Zealand's 52–26 win in Cardiff last November was their 34th consecutive win over Wales. Tom Rogers became the first Wales player to score a hat-trick against them that day, and Wales still lost by 26.
Wales come in on two defeats, the last of them 0–43 to South Africa in July. New Zealand put 50 and then 43 on Australia in October.

New Zealand are level with South Africa on 15 points at the top of the Nations Championship, separated only by points difference, so the margin matters to them as much as the result. A Wales win would lift them to ninth in the world, above Fiji.
Thousands of tickets were still available in early November, with fans boycotting the Principality Stadium. Those staying away have seen how this one usually ends.

espn-604002.headline: Borthwick's job is safe. England's ranking is not
beats: Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, has backed Steve Borthwick through to next year's World Cup even if England flop in the Nations Championship. The backing landed alongside a Times article portraying players fed up with his man-management, and Jamie George saying the squad would "fight to protect" him.

On paper Japan are the gentle stretch of November. England beat Fiji 73–8 and Argentina 31–24 in July, though their year also holds an 18–23 defeat away to Italy. Japan beat Fiji in September, lost to them 28–34 in October and conceded 56 to Australia in August.
A Japan win would send England down to seventh, below Scotland and Australia, which is roughly what a flop looks like when it is written down.
New Zealand come to England a week later. Nobody wants to test that backing before they arrive.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland can only lose ground to Fiji in Dublin
beats: Ireland have been third in the world every week since July. A draw at the Aviva with the side ranked ninth would hand that place to France.
Fiji are bottom of the Nations Championship without a point, and lost 8–73 to England at home in July. Their last game was a 34–28 win in Japan in October.
Joey Carbery won the last of his 38 caps against Fiji in 2022. He is named in the Ireland XV to face Fiji A in Cork on 20 November, the night before Ireland host South Africa.
Captain Dan Sheehan calls talk of a decline in Irish rugby "nonsense". Slipping behind France after a draw with Fiji would be hard to file under the same word.

espn-604004.headline: Sixth and seventh, and they swapped in October
beats: Australia held sixth until 19 October. In the fortnight before it, they conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand, and Scotland moved up without playing.

Neither side gets a gentle run-in. Scotland first meet New Zealand, still chasing their first win over them. Australia first go to Twickenham to play England, while a pay dispute with Rugby Australia runs a year out from a home World Cup.
History leans one way: 22 Australian wins to Scotland's 13 in 35 meetings, including 16 in a row after Scotland won at Ballymore in 1982.
Win at Murrayfield and Scotland go up to fifth, above England, the side Australia will just have played.
